stem:
Aisha joins the school astronomy club on the rooftop. Over two hours she sees the Pole Star stay nearly fixed while other stars seem to drift around it.

Why does the Pole Star appear nearly stationary?

options.text: Earth's rotation axis points very close to the Pole Star.
Other stars actually orbit the Pole Star.
Stars circling the Pole Star make Earth rotate.
The Pole Star is the nearly fixed centre of star trails in both hemispheres.

teacher.key_rationale: Earth's rotation axis points near the Pole Star in the Northern Hemisphere, so it looks fixed. Actual orbits, stars causing Earth's spin, or both-hemisphere visibility miss that.
